Every one of the **119 tools** carries a posture, and every call is judged against it before it runs. This page is generated from the configuration itself rather than described, because a description of it kept being wrong.

> These are the **shipped defaults**. Every value here lives in a config
> file you own once TESSERACT is installed, so your copy may differ — and
> should, once you tune it.


## What stops and asks

These **18** tools prompt every time they are used:

| `agent_promote` |

## What runs without asking

The remaining **101** run automatically. Most are reads — searching memory, listing a directory, looking something up. Some are not, and those are the ones worth knowing about: sending on a channel you connected, handing work to a CLI you already pay for, writing to the assistant's own memory. Setting those up was the decision; being asked again each time would be noise.

## Two things that surprise people

**Read-only commands do not prompt.** 10 command patterns — running the tests, asking git what changed — are allowed in every mode. A prompt for `git status` is noise, and noise is what teaches people to click through prompts without reading them.

**There is more than one mode.** The shipped default is `max`, and there are 3 in total. A headless mode exists for unattended work and relaxes writes and commands; it is not the default and turning it on is a deliberate act.

## Paths beat tools

A tool's posture is not the last word. Path rules apply on top, and they can refuse what the tool alone would allow — the assistant cannot write to its own permissions file, to the runtime's source, or to `.env`, whatever `file_write` says. See `config/permissions.yaml` for the full list; it ships with the app.
